title: What If You Could Hibernate Like a Bear?
description:
You curl up in November, close your eyes, and wake up in spring. No food, no water, no bathroom breaks. Bears do this every winter, and somehow walk out of their dens strong. Here's what hibernating would really be like for you, the primate that already does it, the hidden "hibernation switch" found in mice, and why it might be how humans finally get to Mars.

If you could sleep through every winter, would you do it? Tell me in the comments 👇

SOURCES
• Black bear hibernation: heart rate under 20 bpm, sometimes under 10; urea recycling; little muscle or bone loss
• NASA: astronauts lose about 1–1.5% of bone mass per month in space
• Dausmann et al., Nature 2004: the fat-tailed dwarf lemur hibernates
• Takahashi et al., Nature 2020: Q neurons induce a torpor-like state in mice
• Targeted temperature management after cardiac arrest
• ESA and NASA/SpaceWorks studies of torpor for Mars crews
